title: Eleven Terms and One Unclaimed Scroll
subtitle: 成功与成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功与成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功与成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：degree　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 degree 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the registrar ① awarded a degree that no college in the city would have recognised, and he said the awarding was the whole of the ceremony. The ② degree, meaning the qualification and not the level, ran eleven terms and stayed unclaimed in the office; a degree, he said, is the only thing in a college that is judged by how long it is left uncollected.

Every ③ degree in that college had the same unclaimed scroll beside it, and the ④ degree at the end, meaning the one they kept for the evening students and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever queried twice. A degree, his clerk said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to award; the registrar said the patience is the part that fills eleven terms.

The physicist meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the degree was the whole of the reading, meaning the level and not the qualification. The ⑥ degree, meaning the level and not any of that, is the only thing in a reading that everybody records and nobody feels; degree, she said, is either something you award or the only word that means both a qualification and a level. She said the level is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ degree had become a line in a calendar, and the calendar had become an argument about the unclaimed scroll. The ⑧ degree of the whole thing, the registrar wrote in June, was one college and eleven terms of awarding; degree, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to award. She said the awarding was never mentioned.

The ⑨ degree I remember is the one at the end, which was collected in 1971 and is still described as the strangest in the college. A ⑩ degree, the clerk said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being earned; every degree, she said, is a level that has agreed to look like a qualification. She said the level was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 学位（指学院里授予的那一个）
B. n. 学位（指那份资格本身，与那个度数相对）
C. 固定搭配：award a degree 授予一个学位
D. n. 学位（指留给夜校生的那一个）
E. n. 学位；学位资格（抽象总称，指一所学院的全部学位）
F. n. 学位（指校历上写到、被排定的那一个）
G. n. 度数；程度（指读到的那个数值）
H. n. 程度（抽象总称，指人人记录却无人感受到的那一档）

items.q: awarded a degree that no college in the city would have recognised
The degree, meaning the qualification and not the level
the degree was the whole of the reading
the degree had become a line in a calendar
The degree of the whole thing
A degree, the clerk said in 1973

answers.why: award a degree 意为“授予一个学位”，1949 年注册主任授予了一个全城没有一所学院肯承认的学位。
degree 意为“学位”，指那份资格本身而不是那个度数，它在办公室里搁了十一个学期无人领取。
degree 意为“学位”，指那所学院里每一个学位，每一个旁边都有同一卷未领的证书。
degree 意为“学位”，指留给夜校生的那一个，是唯一有人查问过两次的。
degree 意为“度数、程度”，指读到的那个数值，物理学家说这个度数就是那次读数的全部。
degree 意为“程度”，指人人记录却无人感受到的那一档而不是那份资格，是读数里人人都记录、却无人感受到的东西。
degree 意为“学位”，指校历上写到、被排定的那一个，到 1958 年这个学位成了校历里的一行。
degree 意为“学位、学位资格”，注册主任六月写道，整件事的学位资格是一所学院和十一个学期的授予。
degree 意为“学位”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1971 年被领走，至今仍被说成学院里最奇的一个。
degree 为抽象总称，书记员 1973 年说，一个学位是唯一会因为被挣得而变得更好的东西。
